I bought a small item from Amazon about a month ago, costing around $10. The item arrived quickly and was as nice as I expected. Inside the package, there was a note from the seller. The note said that if I left a 5-star review and then sent them an email to a specific Hotmail address, they'd send me a free item. I'm pretty sure that's against Amazon's seller policies. But I decided to email them anyway, pretending I left a review and wanted my gift. I didn't actually leave a review, and I still haven't. They responded positively, and today I received the gift, which was a second one of the same exact item. Now, I checked on this seller and saw that they have over 1000 seller ratings, and 100% were positive. So it's not like they're a brand-new seller, and I can't imagine they haven't been doing this for a while. Inside today's package was a thank you for my review (again, I haven't left one) and a reminder that on all the items they sell, a 5-star review equals a free item. My question is, would it be wrong (WIBTA) if I were to report them to Amazon after receiving my free item like that? If so, what should I do instead? Alright, so first, I need to understand what's going on here. The seller is offering free items in exchange for 5-star reviews. That seems like they're trying to manipulate reviews to make their product look better. I think Amazon has policies against this because it can mislead other buyers. But I went along with it, pretending to leave a review to get a free item. Now I have the free item, and I'm considering whether to report them. Is that morally acceptable? I guess one thing to consider is whether I'm complicit in their actions by accepting the free item. By taking the free item, am I supporting their unethical behavior? Or am I just taking advantage of a situation that's already there? Also, if I report them, would that be fair? They've been doing this for a while, and all their reviews are positive. Maybe they've been getting away with it because no one has reported them yet. On the other hand, if I don't report them, am I letting them continue to manipulate reviews and possibly harm the integrity of Amazon's review system? I'm also thinking about the consequences for me. If I report them, could they take action against me? Or would Amazon appreciate the information to enforce their policies? Another angle is whether I should have just refused the free item and not participated in their scheme in the first place. But I already did, so what's the best course of action now? Maybe I should consider the bigger picture. If everyone just took the free items without reporting, the seller would keep getting away with it. But if I report them, it might help Amazon to address the issue and prevent others from doing the same. However, I'm also wondering if there's a more ethical way to handle this. Perhaps I could contact the seller and explain that their actions are against Amazon's policies and ask them to stop. But I'm not sure if that would be effective. Alternatively, I could just leave a honest review, explaining my experience with their offer, but that might not be necessary since I haven't left a review yet. Overall, I'm torn between wanting to do the right thing by reporting the seller and not wanting to get involved in something that might have negative consequences for me. I need to weigh the moral implications of my actions and decide what aligns best with my values and the rules set by Amazon.
